written.myAnswer: At dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates, so concentrations remain constant. At static equilibrium, no ongoing change or movement occurs.
Choose conditions that favour the product side and remove product(s) as they form.
Add a catalyst. It increases the rates of both forward and reverse reactions, so equilibrium is reached sooner.
There is no change in the equilibrium position because there are equal numbers of moles of gas on both sides of the equation.
(a) Add reactants or remove products to drive the reaction forward. (b) Add products or remove reactants to drive it backward.
A catalyst increases the rates of both forward and reverse reactions and reduces the time to reach equilibrium, but does not change the equilibrium position.
Remove one or more products from the reaction mixture as they form.

Increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction; decreasing temperature favours the exothermic direction. Since ammonia formation is exothermic, increasing temperature favours the backward reaction and decreasing temperature favours the forward reaction.

Use high pressure, which favours the side with fewer gas molecules (ammonia); use a lower temperature because ammonia formation is exothermic; and remove or liquefy ammonia as it forms. A catalyst speeds up the attainment of equilibrium but does not increase the equilibrium yield.
